town.name: Mueang Kanchanaburi (Kanchanaburi town, where the Khwae Noi and Khwae Yai meet)

households.home: farm house on a sugarcane and cassava plot
households.livelihood: grows sugarcane (about 4.39 million tonnes province-wide), cassava and rice, the province's largest sector at about 25% of output

households.home: rented row house near a sugar mill
households.livelihood: works in manufacturing, the second-largest sector at 24.4%, which includes the Mitr Kasetr sugar mill

households.home: wooden house in a mining district

landmarks.name: Erawan Falls
landmarks.note: Seven pools stepping down a forested hill, the water leaving through three spouts shaped like the heads of the white elephant Erawan.

landmarks.name: Confluence of the Khwae Noi and Khwae Yai into the Mae Klong
landmarks.note: Two rivers meeting at the edge of a mountain range beside the town.

landmarks.name: Mueang Sing Historical Park (Prasat Muang Sing)
landmarks.note: A Khmer-era temple site of laterite and stone, no build year given in source.

note: New archetype: a Gulf-of-Thailand province of palm-sugar groves, salt pans and a coast resort, with mountains behind. Also used for Prachuap Khiri Khan.

households.livelihood: palm sugar, Ban Lat district specialises in it; the province has more sugar palms than any other

households.home: house beside salt pans on the coast
households.livelihood: salt farming, 137 families worked 9,880 rai in 2011 (Ban Laem is known for salt and seafood)

households.home: shophouse near the Cha-am beach strip

landmarks.name: Wat Ko Kaeo Suttharam
landmarks.note: Central-Thai temple with interior murals dated to about 1734-35.

landmarks.name: Tanaosi Range and Kaeng Krachan forest
landmarks.note: Forested ridge on the Myanmar border, in Thailand's largest national park, covering nearly half the province.

landmarks.name: Cha-am beach
landmarks.note: Gulf shore beach resort, being eroded by the sea.

nameTh: ประจวบคีรีขันธ์

town.name: Bang Saphan (Ban Krut area, Gulf coast; a different town from Hua Hin)

households.home: wooden house in a coconut grove
households.livelihood: coconut farming, about 40% of the province's farmers grow only coconuts

households.home: village house in Ban Huai Kriab
households.livelihood: black-and-white rattan basketry, a weaving group of 38 members running nine shops

households.home: hut by a stream in Ban Pa Ron
households.livelihood: gold panning in Klong Thong stream, which locals still do

landmarks.name: Ban Krut beach
landmarks.note: Long Gulf of Thailand beach with a few bungalow resorts.

landmarks.name: Tenasserim Hills
landmarks.note: A wall of hills along the western horizon on the Myanmar border.

landmarks.name: Khao Sam Roi Yot
landmarks.note: Limestone peaks rising from the shore, up to 605 m, beside Thailand's largest freshwater marsh.

households.home: wooden house on a canal bank
households.livelihood: sells fruit and vegetables from a small wooden sampan on the canals (the vendors wear blue mo hom shirts and straw hats)
sells food and souvenirs to day-trip visitors, busiest 7 to 9 in the morning

landmarks.name: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market
landmarks.note: A maze of narrow canals crowded with sampans of produce, later covered by a roof; the modern market began in 1981.

landmarks.name: Khao Bin cave
landmarks.note: Limestone cave where large bat colonies swarm out in the evening.

landmarks.name: Kaeng Som Maew
landmarks.note: A large stone islet in the Phachi River.

households.home: bamboo and timber house in a Karen hill village
households.livelihood: hill-tribe farming; Karen are the largest hill tribe in Tak, and about a quarter of the province's people belong to hill tribes

households.home: rented room near a garment factory
households.livelihood: migrant family from Myanmar working in factories and garment workshops; the town's local industries rely heavily on Burmese workers
cross-border trade with Myanmar, mainly wholesale gems and teak, plus textiles and jade

landmarks.name: Thai-Myanmar Friendship Bridge
landmarks.note: Road bridge over the Moei River to Myawaddy, opened in 1997.

landmarks.name: Moei River
landmarks.note: The border river that the Friendship Bridge crosses.

landmarks.name: Thi Lo Su Waterfall
landmarks.note: Large waterfall in the south of the province, a seasonal ecotourism spot.
